outcome: An object's power, toughness, types, colors, abilities and controller are the result of applying all continuous effects to its printed values in layer order.
Copy effects and other copiable-value modifications apply first, before any other layer.
A control-changing effect gives a permanent a new controller before later layers evaluate.
A text-changing effect alters a land type or color word before later layers evaluate.
A type-changing effect changes a permanent's card types and subtypes before later layers, so effects keyed to type apply or stop applying.
A color-changing effect changes a permanent's colors before later layers, so effects keyed to color apply or stop applying.
Granted or removed abilities and keywords change a permanent's keyword list before power and toughness effects.
Power and toughness effects apply last and determine the final power and toughness.
Layer 1 effects apply in sublayer order, then timestamp order within a sublayer.
A copy effect sets the copy's copiable values, and later effects apply on top of them.
A face-down permanent has the characteristics of a 2/2 nameless creature with no abilities.
After layer 1 the object's characteristics are its copiable values, which a copy of it would take.
Within layers 2 to 6, characteristic-defining abilities apply before other effects, which apply in timestamp order.
Layer 7 effects apply in sublayer order, then timestamp order within a sublayer.
A characteristic-defining power or toughness is applied first in layer 7.
An effect that sets power or toughness overrides earlier values and the base used by later modifiers.
Pump effects and +1/+1 counters add to the power and toughness set in layer 7b regardless of timestamp.
A switch effect swaps the power and toughness computed so far, and later modifiers apply to the switched values.
Layer results update instantly, so a permanent's characteristics change as soon as an effect's applicability changes.
A multi-part effect applies each part in its own layer to the same set of objects, even if those objects no longer match the original condition.
Within a layer, the effect with the earlier timestamp applies first and the later one wins on conflict.
A static ability's effect has the timestamp of its object or of the effect that granted the ability, whichever is later.
An effect created by a resolving spell or ability is timestamped at resolution.
Putting a counter of a kind on an object gives all counters of that kind the new timestamp.
An object that changes zones gets a new timestamp, so effects it grants or receives order after existing ones.
Attaching an Aura or Equipment gives it a new timestamp, which changes who wins a conflict with other effects.
Turning a permanent face up or face down gives it a new timestamp.
Transforming a double-faced permanent gives it a new timestamp.

note: Plane and scheme cards belong to casual variants, which are not played in collection
Conspiracy cards act at the start of the game and in drafts, which collection does not use
No sticker card exists in Forge's cardsfolder
Only the active player's choice of relative order differs from fixed timestamps

outcome: When a permanent enters with characteristics set by an effect, its own static ability is timestamped earlier than the resolving effect's.
A dependency between effects in the same layer overrides timestamp order.
An effect depends on another when applying the other would change its text, existence or the objects it affects.
A dependent effect applies just after the effects it depends on, and a dependency loop falls back to timestamp order.
After each applied effect, dependencies among the remaining effects are re-evaluated and the order may change.
One effect overrides another, and a later-timestamp effect wins, such as an Aura that adds flying versus one that removes it.
Effects on players, such as protection from a color, apply in timestamp order after object characteristics are determined.
Effects on game rules, such as maximum hand size or must-attack, apply after all other continuous effects.
